Between requests, everything before S is identical (0.1x read) — but S is at a fixed history offset (say 10.3k tokens worth of history). Everything after S in request N was written at 1.25x on request N; on request N+1, if the developer item's position relative to the post-S content hasn't changed, that region should hit...

The only way the pin persists forever (E2: "permanently") is if the developer item's position differs between consecutive requests — i.e., case: request N's developer item at position p_N, request N+1's at position p_{N+1}, p_N ≠ p_{N+1} alternates (e.g., user-turn request: before the last user item; tool-loop request: at the tail). That's the "pin": the cache-hit length never grows past the swap point, and the write region = (history after the swap point) + tail = 113-1,004 tokens at the time of measurement, growing over time.

Also, the 32MB body cap (N2) must stay.

3. **Don't pre-expose all MCP tools in the initial request to eliminate discovery turns.** It would push the tool array into the cache prefix; MCP tool schemas are large (hundreds to thousands of tokens each), and the tool array is part of the request body that gets cached; any MCP server reconnect / tool change invalidates the whole prefix for the whole session (tools are serialized before input in the request — a change busts everything). The current lazy discovery keeps the prefix small and stable; the fix is to reduce per-tool discovery cost, not to front-load.

4. **Don't make `parallel_tool_calls: true` the default "because the model parallelizes."** E5/E1: the harness is already parallelizing under the API default, yet still 2.9x the turns — parallelism isn't the missing lever, and explicit-false is codex parity; also interleaved `tco_*` reasoning siblings (one per parallel call, replayed verbatim per the code comment in `response_to_conversation_items`) bloat replay size and add ordering risk.
